## Lane 2 — PASS (confidence 0.94)
Reviewed baseline d2cf18438debba60d87ce46ba6da68bca6f072b3 plus implementation-review.diff, supplied SHA256 8e5beba17e58c94b7db47611c9192227ea580a6480b46011be5cce6420c2fc4c; no confirmed patch-introduced boundary defect or concrete fix required.

Path abbreviations: C = crates/honk-core/src/control/routing_matcher/codegen.rs; P = crates/honk-core/src/control/routing_matcher.rs; B = crates/honk-core/src/ebpf/real/routing.rs; R = crates/honk-ebpf/src/route.rs.

### Mandatory negative-space accounting
| Path | Counted? | Bounded? | Intentional? / source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Category absent from policy | Yes: static count 0 | Zero acquisition, zero cache stores | Yes; C:59-91 |
| Category appears once | Yes: static count 1 | At most one reached lookup, no cache state | Yes; C:75-91,649-652 |
| Category appears at least twice | Yes: saturating count 2 | Two entry DW stores; at most one acquisition attempt per invocation | Yes; C:297-300,637-648 |
| First textual occurrence short-circuited | Yes: ready remains 0 | Later first reached occurrence acquires once | Yes; C:316-330,640-645 |
| Category never reached because an earlier rule returns | Yes | Zero category lookups; repeated categories still pay two initialization stores each | Yes; C:297-300,324-329 |
| Earlier condition fails within a rule | Yes | Shared fail label skips remaining conditions without changing their cache state | Yes; C:317-330,436-449 |
| Lookup returns NULL | Yes: pointer=0 plus ready=1 | No later retry; no bitmap dereference | Yes; C:642-647,620-624 |
| Non-NULL all-zero bitmap | Yes: positive pointer retained | Each reached predicate reads its own bit; distinct from NULL internally | Yes; C:620-624,643-647 |
| Invalid family, including 0 and 3 | Yes: completed absent acquisition | Zero LPM helpers; cached NULL when repeated | Yes; C:676-689 |
| MAC absent | Yes: completed absent acquisition | Zero LPM helpers; cached NULL when repeated | Yes; C:664-689 |
| Present all-zero MAC | Yes | One actual MAC lookup, because presence is separate from key bytes | Yes; C:664-666; R:232-234 |
| Negated fact | Yes: same category accounting | Tests the positive bit, then swaps pass/fail; never caches a negated result | Yes; C:444-447,620-624 |
| Domain predicate | Explicit exception | Exactly one entry domain lookup when domain metadata is present; none otherwise | Yes: also controls domain_final; C:303-313,460-461 |
| Scalar, port, DSCP, process predicate | Outside cache by design | No fact-map helper; emitted expansion remains under assembler limits | Yes; C:59-65,495-609 |
| Other helper between first use and reuse | Yes | Only map_lookup_elem is emitted; R6/R7/R8 and DW stack spills preserve retained state | Yes; C:285-309,640-647,694-704 |
| NULL input/output pointer | Before initialization | Immediate -EFAULT, no acquisition | Yes; C:278-283 |
| Final fallback / next invocation | Yes | Exit discards the frame; every new invocation initializes its own enabled slots | Yes; C:297-300,333-335 |
| Root/descriptor lookup | Outside fact-cache scope | Two wrapper map helpers; missing root/descriptor returns before the evaluator | Yes; R:123-147; Aya ArrayOfMaps::get_value source linked below |
| Cached-flow / earlier datapath bypass | Outside evaluator scope | No generated invocation, hence no generated fact acquisition | Yes; ingress.rs:688-700; no claim that unrelated conntrack/parser helpers are included |
| Other emitter entry points | Closed | Production publication and test-only emission use the same emitter; no alternate fact lookup consumer | B:328-329; routing/tests.rs:852-854,959-964 |

Derived helper ceiling: destination ≤1, source ≤1, MAC ≤1, domain ≤1, therefore generated evaluator ≤4 map_lookup_elem calls per invocation; canonical root/slot path ≤6, excluding parser/conntrack and test-fixture input/output helpers.

### Dispatch symmetry: producer → actual map/key/bit consumer
| Category | Plan producer | FD consumer and lookup key |
|---|---|---|
| Destination | P:135-144,349-369 | B:250-251,262-263 → C:463-472,670-684; IPv4 destination bytes 12..15 with /32 key, IPv6 destination bytes 0..15 with /128 key |
| Source | P:145-154,349-369 | B:252-253,264-265 → C:474-483,670-684; corresponding source bytes, never destination bytes |
| MAC | P:155-161,373-376 | B:254,266 → C:485-494,664-666; canonical 16 bytes, six MAC bytes at 10..15, /128 key |
| Domain | B:245-247,267 | C:303-309; full 16-byte destination hash key, pointer retained in R8 |

Reverse audit: every fact lookup arm has a FactKind classification and matching cache index; the source-default arm is nested inside Destination|Source, so MAC cannot fall into it (C:59-64,463-494,662-685). Every allowed ID reaches the actual DomainRouting word at 4×floor(id/32), mask 1<<(id%32), with IDs <256 ensuring byte range 0..31 (C:372-383,620-624; honk-ebpf-common/src/redirect_need.rs:69-73); parent-prefix inheritance and duplicate OR make one longest-prefix result contain every relevant positive fact bit (P:381-418).

### Stack intervals and initialization
| Storage | Exact inclusive byte interval | Initialization / access |
|---|---|---|
| Domain key | [-96,-81] | Two DW stores before domain helper; C:726-731 |
| MAC pointer / ready | [-80,-73] / [-72,-65] | Separate aligned DW slots; C:87-90,299-300 |
| LPM key | [-64,-45] | Prefix W plus four initialized data W words; C:712-722 |
| Unused gap | [-44,-33] | No accesses |
| Source pointer / ready | [-32,-25] / [-24,-17] | Separate aligned DW slots |
| Destination pointer / ready | [-16,-9] / [-8,-1] | Separate aligned DW slots |

No overlap, including full-width spills; enabled caches consume exactly 16 bytes each, at most 48 bytes, and maximum generated frame depth remains 96 bytes with domain or 80 bytes for repeated MAC without domain. All helper key bytes are initialized before use, all cache slots are initialized before domain or fact helpers, and the cache pointer is stored before publishing ready=1 (C:297-308,643-644,712-731).

### Instruction, branch and state ceilings
Static instruction-slot derivation, counting LD_IMM64 as two slots and labels as zero: IPv4 key+lookup 13; IPv6/MAC key+lookup 19; fact selection 39 for IP or 23 for MAC; bitmap test 5; enabled cache wrapper 6 (C:613-735).

| Condition | Uncached slots / jumps | Cached slots / jumps |
|---|---:|---:|
| Destination/source | 44 / 8 | 50 / 10 |
| MAC | 28 / 5 | 34 / 7 |
| Domain | 5 / 3 | Unchanged R8 path |

Each enabled category adds two prologue stores; domain presence adds 13 static entry slots; the remaining fixed prologue/fallback contributes 15 slots and each emitted rule contributes six success/exit slots (C:278-335). Compared with the baseline, single-use IP emits two fewer static slots and single-use MAC two more: no cache state does not imply byte-identical code or a zero instruction delta on every path.

The runtime CFG is forward-only; each enabled ready flag transitions 0→1 at most once, yielding at most eight readiness combinations, but this is NOT an eight-state verifier bound because distinct lookup sites, nullable pointer identities, family branches and predicate constraints also matter. The emitter rejects insertion beyond 1,000,000 slots and rejects out-of-i16 jump offsets, while kernel processed-instruction/state rejection remains a separate load-time ceiling with diagnostic errors before root publication (C:156-199; B:197-212,328-356); the supplied packed-ready rejection log explicitly reports 1,000,001 processed instructions, whereas the current DW-ready host and Linux 6.12 logs each report 7/7 routing tests passing, not universal policy acceptance.

### Immutable generation ownership and stale-pointer attack
Five static fact maps are filled only during candidate construction, then moved into private generation-owned fields; only domain has an active mutation accessor (B:30-49,233-267,359-385; real/mod.rs:529-575). No new allocation, refcount, shared cache, map write, tail call, or helper capable of invalidating packet pointers is introduced: cached pointers remain invocation-local, helper-clobbered R0-R5 are never relied on across calls, and every bitmap load is preceded by its NULL branch (C:620-624,637-704).

The unchanged publication boundary retains the active generation while constructing candidate maps/program/links, publishes the descriptor root last, and drops the previous generation only after that update returns (B:319-375). The Linux 6.12 source independently confirms successful map_update_elem calls maybe_wait_bpf_programs, whose ARRAY_OF_MAPS path runs synchronize_rcu; candidate and active ownership remain at most two generations in this serialized backend path, with no added per-policy map resource and unchanged map-capacity errors.

### Hostile second pass / evidence classification
DEFEND: skipped-first-use initialization, cached NULL versus zero bitmap, alternating IPv4/IPv6/MAC values, source/destination dispatch symmetry, helper-clobber survival, full-width stack overlap, and generation retirement all survive direct source tracing; no confirmed defect and no newly discovered pre-existing issue. REFINE: eight readiness combinations and a four-helper evaluator bound do not prove arbitrary policies stay below the verifier budget, and single-use no-cache paths are not instruction-identical to baseline; no lab ARM/x86, full-traffic, dynamic-helper-count or broader-kernel PASS claimed from this read-only review.

Boundary design quality 9/10; boundary merge readiness 9/10, conditional on the other lanes and outstanding separately authorized gates rather than an overall merge recommendation. No builds, tests, runtime probes or edits performed by this lane.

External source links: https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v6.12/kernel/bpf/syscall.c#L149-L162 and #L1630-L1632; https://docs.rs/crate/aya-ebpf/0.2.0/source/src/btf_maps/of_maps/array.rs.
